tools.title: Native API Call
tools.description: Read a low-risk Revit API member through gateway guardrails using direct JSON arguments. Body: {memberId,target?:uiapp|uidoc|doc|view,args?:[],dryRun?}.

tools.title: Native API Read-Only Operations
tools.description: Compose up to 16 low-risk reflected constructor, static, instance, or public-property reads with ephemeral per-request result references. Targets may be uiapp|uidoc|doc|view or $priorId; arguments may reference a prior result as {$ref:'priorId'}. Body: {operations:[{id,op:construct|call|get_property,memberId?,property?,target?,args?:[]}],returns?:[$id],maxTotalMs?:250..10000,maxOperationMs?:100..10000}. V2 remains read-only and rejects mutating, freeze-risk, and non-low-risk members.
tools.example: count sheets with a FilteredElementCollector operation chain
common_errors: Unsupported parameter type: Autodesk.Revit.DB.Document: supply a typed Document result with an argument $ref; neither a bare $doc string nor omitting the first argument binds that position.
notes: Arguments are positional in the reflected signature. Use an object {"$ref":"earlierOperationId"} to pass an earlier operation's typed result; a string such as "$doc" is a literal, not an argument reference. To pass the active Document, first get_property with target:"uidoc", property:"Document", then use {"$ref":"thatOperationId"} in its argument position. Omitting a leading context argument does not shift later arguments. References exist only within this request.

A target is uiapp, uidoc, doc, view, or $earlierOperationId. Static calls must omit target. Argument references use an object with $ref, whereas target references use a string starting with $. The referenced runtime type must match the parameter type; an Element result can also supply an ElementId parameter.

args.description: Arguments are positional in the reflected signature. tools.title: Native API Transaction Operations
tools.description: Execute up to 16 reflected operations inside one explicit Revit transaction. Supports generic 3D placeholder solids: construct lines/arcs, CurveLoop.Create, CreateExtrusionGeometry, then DirectShape.CreateElement and SetShape. Use graph_allowed member ids and typed prior-result arguments {$ref:'id'}, including collection arguments such as [[{$ref:'curve_a'},{$ref:'curve_b'}]]; target:$id selects an instance. References exist only within this request. Supported detached geometry is bounded to the documented factories and Curve/CurveLoop/Solid/GeometryObject references, not arbitrary objects or ShapeBuilder. Nested collections are bounded; see the generic one-foot placeholder example. This high-risk route requires a write grant, at least one persisted model mutation, active-document ownership, a 1..64 affected-element cap, and explicit commit or rollback. Choose commit for authorized application; rollback is optional preview or an explicit user request. A generic solid has no MEP connectors or inferred service. At the real transaction boundary, a document-scoped Dynamic Model Updater observes affected ids and failure processing verifies the in-scope commit or rollback. Body: {operations:[{id,op:construct|call|get_property,memberId?,property?,target?,args?:[]}],returns?:[$id],transaction:{mode:rollback|commit,name?,maxAffectedElements,allowCreate?,allowedExistingElementIds?:[]},maxTotalMs?:250..10000,maxOperationMs?:100..10000}.
tools.example: create a generic 3D placeholder box or cylinder using native solid geometry
common_errors: Unsupported parameter type: Autodesk.Revit.DB.Document: supply a typed Document result with an argument $ref; neither a bare $doc string nor omitting the first argument binds that position.
notes: Arguments are positional in the reflected signature. To pass the active Document, first get_property with target:"uidoc", property:"Document", then use {"$ref":"thatOperationId"} in its argument position. Omitting a leading context argument does not shift later arguments. References exist only within this request.

The referenced runtime type must match the parameter type; an Element result can also supply an ElementId parameter.

For graph_allowed native geometry signatures, collection arguments may contain typed prior-result references, for example args:[[{$ref:'edge_a'},{$ref:'edge_b'}]]. Geometry references are limited to Curve, CurveLoop, Solid and GeometryObject; supported detached factories are Line.CreateBound, three-XYZ Arc.Create, CurveLoop.Create and three-argument CreateExtrusionGeometry. DirectShape.CreateElement/SetShape are document mutations inside this graph's transaction. Collections are bounded to 64 items and depth 4, with a shared 256-node argument budget. See the one-foot generic 3D placeholder example; these graph-only signatures do not work through native-api-call.

tools.title: State Snapshot
tools.description: Capture a stable, read-only Revit session snapshot for planning/verification. Body: {include_dialogs?,include_selection_details?,include_sheet_viewports?,include_all_views_index?,include_warnings_summary?,include_warnings_detail?,include_element_bboxes?,max_items?}.

notes: Core snapshot fields are always present; unsupported values resolve as null.

Defaults: include_dialogs=true, include_selection_details=true, include_sheet_viewports=true, include_all_views_index=false, include_warnings_summary=true, include_warnings_detail=false, include_element_bboxes=false.

tools.title: Open Model
tools.description: Open and activate a Revit model from disk in the currently running Revit session. Body: {filePath,audit?,detach?,discardExistingOpenDocument?,continueOnUnresolvedReferences?}. Detach preserves worksets when enabled. If the exact document is already open but inactive, or is loaded as a link in an open host, activation requires discardExistingOpenDocument=true. That flag authorizes closing the inactive document without saving or unloading the exact link type before opening it as a top-level document, and must be explicitly authorized. When continueOnUnresolvedReferences=true, the bridge pre-arms a one-shot guard that selects 'Ignore and continue opening the project' only for Revit's Unresolved References dialog containing the missing-reference message; use it only with explicit authorization to continue despite missing references. If the user requested a specific Revit year, launch/verify that Revit version first and call this only from that session; do not open RVTs through Windows file association.
tools.example: open model C:\\Projects\\Sample.rvt

tools.title: Close Active Model
tools.description: Post Revit's native Close Active Project command after the current API event, keep Revit running, and verify the document transition separately. Body: {discardUnsavedChanges?:bool}. A modified document is not closed unless discardUnsavedChanges=true; when explicitly authorized, a narrow one-shot dialog guard selects No on Revit's save-changes prompt.
tools.example: close the active disposable sample model without saving

tools.title: Save As Model
tools.description: Save the active model to a new path. Body: {filePath,overwrite?,compact?,maximumBackups?,saveAsCentral?,dryRun?}. Relative paths resolve against active document directory (or Workspace when unsaved).
tools.example: save model as Coordination_Copy.rvt

tools.title: Rooms
tools.description: List rooms/spaces or fetch room/space details. Request: {action:"list"|"detail", levelName?, roomIds?, roomNumber?, max?, viewId?, includeBoundaryElementIds?, spatialKindPreference?:"auto"|"room"|"space"}. Detail responses include true boundaryLoops plus boundary.sideClassification helpers in view basis for deterministic left/right/top/bottom wall selection.
tools.example: find room 0981
notes: Use spatialKindPreference=space when a room number is known to resolve to an MEP Space instead of an architectural Room.
detail with roomNumber + spatialKindPreference resolves deterministically without a separate /revit/spaces endpoint.

tools.title: Linked Room Boundaries
tools.description: Read-only extraction of linked architectural Room.GetBoundarySegments loops transformed into host coordinates. POST is used for filters only; no write grant is required. Body: {levelName?, linkedModelNameContains?, roomNumber?, roomNameContains?, maxRooms?, includeBoundarySegmentMetadata?}.
tools.example: extract linked room boundaries on LEVEL 03

tools.title: Find Elements by Category
tools.description: Count placed elements by category and group returned family and type only when itemsComplete is true. A truncated result is not a complete inventory. Selector helper: find element ids by scope (viewId OR sheetNumber) and filters. Supports sheet-region targeting, visible-text search, and bounded document discovery across instance name, family, type, category, and Mark. identityTerms uses exact phrase or at-least-half meaningful-token overlap and returns the matched evidence. physicalElementsOnly excludes view-owned/non-model artifacts; topLevelInstancesOnly excludes nested children. expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters performs a second, category-grounded scan for delimiter-bounded phrase acronyms in string parameters and returns the exact parameter evidence; it never expands without a first-pass physical identity seed. includeGeometry adds each physical result's world-space location, axis-aligned bounding box, orientation, type, level, host, and location-curve length/straightness. Agent projections expose routeCurveCandidates for bounded duct/pipe edit discovery; connector topology must still be verified before mutation. Body: {viewId?,sheetNumber?,includeSheetElements?,includeViewportElements?,sheetRegions?:[{minU,minV,maxU,maxV}],regionPaddingFt?,category?,categories?,typeNameContains?,familyNameContains?,nameContains?,markContains?,textContains?,identityTerms?:string[],physicalElementsOnly?,topLevelInstancesOnly?,expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters?,includeGeometry?,limit?}.
tools.example: find physical air-terminal instances with world geometry anywhere in this project
notes: Scope precedence: if viewId is provided it is used; otherwise sheetNumber scopes to views placed on that sheet (viewports).
For redline workflows, provide sheetRegions (sheet UV boxes) to return only elements overlapping mapped markup areas.
Categories are BuiltInCategory tokens like OST_Doors, OST_TitleBlocks, OST_GenericModel.

For ordinary whole-document object discovery, identityTerms searches instance name, family, type, category, and Mark while preserving matched-term/field evidence; combine physicalElementsOnly and topLevelInstancesOnly to exclude schedules, legends, annotations, and nested child components.

expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters is seed-gated: only categories with a physical first-pass identity match are scanned for delimiter-bounded phrase acronyms in string parameters, and exact parameter-name/value evidence is returned.

includeGeometry=true returns model/world coordinates, transformed axis-aligned bounding boxes, FamilyInstance facing/hand orientation, and type/level/host ids for bounded project-wide spatial analysis without requiring a visible view export.

tools.title: Update Parameter By Query
tools.description: Find elements by category/text filters, inspect one parameter, and set a new value only when blank or matching the query criteria. Supports preview/apply reporting for repetitive parameter-fill tasks. Body: {category?,categories?,matchStartsWith?,matchContains?,matchParameterNames?,familyNameContains?,typeNameContains?,parameterName,value,onlyWhenBlank?,dryRun?,apply?,confirm?,limit?}.
tools.example: dry-run fill blank A.I.C. Rating for electrical panels whose panel name starts with P

tools.title: Get Placement Context
tools.description: Return host-aware placement diagnostics for one element, including insertion point, type/family, orientation/flip state, exact serializable host-face and linked-element evidence when Revit exposes it, wall-host projection, requested room-side wall context, ranked nearby hosts, circuit membership, and read-only electrical distribution-system evidence for electrical equipment. Body: {elementId,hostCategories?,hostSearchRadiusFt?,maxNearbyHosts?,pointXyz?,roomNumber?,roomSide?}.
tools.example: get placement context for element 12345

tools.title: Create MEP Route
tools.description: Create a multi-segment duct, pipe, or electrical conduit route from ordered XYZ or frame-linked points with dry-run, conservative size/elevation fallbacks, explicit user-workset assignment, internal connector attempts, optional fail-closed endpoint joining, and native readback. Set requiredExistingEndpoint=start|end|both with exact expectedExistingStartOwnerId/expectedExistingEndOwnerId for required ends; an explicit endpoint takes precedence over requireExistingEndpointConnections, while true alone requires both ends. Duplicate duct/pipe/conduit type names fail closed; use ductTypeId, pipeTypeId, or conduitTypeId for stable native selection. Duct profiles and dimensions must be valid and compatible before starting a transaction. Native route size, duct shape, and requested workset readback must match when verify=true. Use dryRun:false for authorized creation and true for a requested preview. Body: {kind:duct|pipe|conduit,frameId?,points:[{x?,y?,z?,xPx?,yPx?,xyz?}],viewId?,roomNumber?,levelName?,levelId?,worksetName?,worksetId?,systemType?,ductType?,ductTypeId?,ductShape?:round|rectangular|oval,pipeType?,pipeTypeId?,conduitType?,conduitTypeId?,ductSize?,diameter?,pipeSize?,segmentSizes?:string[],sizePolicy?:explicit_required|use_default_with_warning,elevationPolicy?:explicit_required|resolve_context_default,routingMode?:orthogonal|polyline,connectSegments?,connectToExisting?,requireExistingEndpointConnections?,requiredExistingEndpoint?:start|end|both,expectedExistingStartOwnerId?,expectedExistingEndOwnerId?,externalConnectionToleranceFt?,verify?,dryRun?}.
tools.example: dry-run a native conduit, pipe, or duct route with three ordered points
notes: A separate preview is optional. When the user has authorized drafting, use dryRun:false to apply directly; honor any explicit read-only or dry-run request. Native authorization, validation, transaction rollback, and connector verification still apply. If size is omitted, default policy uses 8x8 duct or 1 inch pipe and returns a warning.
Use segmentSizes with one size per segment to draft multi-section routes; internal joints with differing adjacent sizes expect transition fittings.
Internal route joints attempt Revit NewTransitionFitting for size changes, otherwise NewElbowFitting, then fall back to Connector.ConnectTo; fitting ids are returned when created.
Connector verification is conservative: created standalone routes normally report open endpoint connectors until connected to equipment or existing runs.

Only points is universally required. For kind=duct use ductType or ductTypeId plus ductSize/diameter; for kind=pipe use pipeType or pipeTypeId plus pipeSize/diameter; for kind=conduit use conduitType or conduitTypeId plus diameter. These alternatives are not simultaneous requirements.

tools.title: Connect Existing MEP Branch
tools.description: Connect one retained branch to the interior of an existing rigid main without replacing accepted geometry. connectionMode:takeoff_fitting creates a native takeoff between one exact open rigid/flex duct or pipe connector and its main, accepts an explicit worksetId/worksetName, and otherwise inherits the retained branch user workset with committed readback. connectionMode:air_terminal_on_duct uses Revit's direct air-terminal attachment operation, requires kind:duct plus an exact open air-terminal connector, and produces the native direct terminal-to-duct topology without an adapter curve. Both modes guard the active model and projected interior point, preserve pre-existing physical connections, verify the result after transaction commit, and perform the real operation inside a rollback-verified transaction group during dry-run. Body: {expectedModelPath?,connectionMode?:takeoff_fitting|air_terminal_on_duct,kind:duct|pipe,mainElementId,branchElementId,branchConnectorId?,expectedBranchOriginXyz?,originToleranceFt?,expectedTakeoffTypeId?,expectedTakeoffFamilyName?,expectedTakeoffTypeName?,worksetId?,worksetName?,dryRun?,verify?}.
tools.example: dry-run attaching an exact retained branch to a rigid main with inherited or explicit workset proof

tools.title: Connect MEP Elements
tools.description: Fail-closed physical connector join for an already placed MEP family/equipment instance and explicit nearby duct, pipe, or family targets. Composes with hosted/unhosted placement, requires compatible open connector shape/domain/size within tolerance, uses one source connector per target, and rolls back if native AllRefs verification does not prove the requested count. Body: {sourceElementId,targetElementIds:[...],toleranceFt?,sizeToleranceFt?,requiredConnectionCount?,dryRun?,verify?}.
tools.example: dry-run connecting a reconstructed air terminal to its explicit open duct target

tools.title: Existing Conditions MEP Draft Workflow
tools.description: Execute one source-grounded reconstruction stage. The Operator harness normally sends one dependency-ready operation per call, but may send a bounded group of explicitly marked independent high-confidence straight backbones. Each stage runs first with dryRun:true and then once with dryRun:false. Later stages pass hash-ledgered priorActionOutputs so accepted native IDs are never replayed. Each call has its own rollback boundary. Responses echo stageKey and persist created_element_ids, affected_element_ids, and route endpoint IDs; the host ledger binds planned continuation endpoints to those IDs and audits their native connectors before acceptance. In addition to route, family, connection, tag, and circuit creation, the wrapper supports repair-first move, rotate, MEP size/elevation edit, and exact connector repair operations against useful existing elements. Body: {stageKey?,priorActionOutputs?:[{action_key,created_element_ids,affected_element_ids?,route_segment_element_ids?,route_start_element_ids?,route_end_element_ids?,split_main_start_element_ids?,split_main_end_element_ids?}],operations:[{action_key,path,depends_on?,apply_body?,deferred_body?,execution_mode?,provisional_batch_key?,continuation_endpoints?}],dryRun?,verify?,maximumCreatedElements?,targetViewId?,applyTargetViewPhase?,requireAllCreatedElementsVisibleInTargetView?}.
tools.example: dry-run one repairable existing-conditions stage or bounded provisional backbone batch, apply it once, verify it, and persist created or affected IDs

tools.title: MEP Route Workflow
tools.description: One-call duct, pipe, or native conduit route workflow that enforces resolve context -> dry-run -> optional apply -> focused post-change highlight/export. Body mirrors create-mep-route, including stable type IDs, explicit worksetName/worksetId, segmentSizes, and optional fail-closed endpoint joining. Set requiredExistingEndpoint=start|end|both with exact expectedExistingStartOwnerId/expectedExistingEndOwnerId; an explicit endpoint takes precedence over requireExistingEndpointConnections, while true alone requires both ends. Plus {apply?:boolean,visualVerify?:boolean,visualViewId?,imageSize?,focusPaddingFt?}. Visual verification is ready only when every created element is found, collected, unhidden, and has a view-specific bounding box in the requested view; otherwise it returns CreatedElementsNotVisibleInView with diagnostics.
tools.example: apply and visually verify a native conduit or duct route
notes: Execution order is fixed: resolve context, dry-run route, apply route only if dry-run is not blocked, then highlight/export the applied elements for visual review.
When apply=false the workflow returns DryRunReady and no visual capture because dry-run elements are rolled back.
When apply=true and visualVerify=true, successful responses include visualVerification.capture.path plus AI review checklist text.
Only points is universally required. Route type, system, shape, and size fields are conditional on kind and may use either stable type IDs or names.

tools.title: MEP Branch Network Workflow
tools.description: One-call network workflow for a main duct/pipe route plus multiple branch tee/tap connections. Dry-run plans the main route, branch projections, selected sizes, retained branch anchors, branch-level reducer/transition joint plans, and accessory/damper graph nodes. Apply creates the main route first, then connects each branch to its requested main segment using /revit/connect-mep-branch; duct tap/takeoff, pipe tap/takeoff with an explicit Revit takeoff/tap routing preference, retained two-connector transition/reducer anchors, and duct/pipe split tee use the lower-level verified guards. A branch with existingBranchAnchorElementId must use connectionMode:"tee" and never falls back to an open-main or tap path. Accessory graph apply supports explicit duct/pipe accessory insertions hosted on created main or branch segments when a compatible loaded or workspace-scoped familyPath symbol resolves, plus explicit target-id duct/pipe accessory delete and type_change with compatible loaded types. Body: {kind:duct|pipe,mainPoints:[...],mainSegmentSizes?,branches:[{mainSegmentIndex,connectionMode?:tee|tap,connectionPoint?,points:[...],branchSize?,branchSegmentSizes?:string[],existingBranchAnchorElementId?}],accessories?:[{action:insert|delete|type_change,targetElementId?,targetElementIds?,typeId?,targetTypeName?,familySymbolId?,familyPath?,familyName?,typeName?,mainSegmentIndex?,branchIndex?,branchSegmentIndex?,chainageFt?,point?}],viewId?,roomNumber?,levelName?,systemType?,ductType?,pipeType?,ductSize?,diameter?,pipeSize?,apply?,verify?,visualVerify?}.
tools.example: dry-run main duct with two branch taps
notes: This workflow drafts a main route plus multiple branch connections by composing /revit/create-mep-route and /revit/connect-mep-branch.
Dry-run plans branch projections and branch-level reducer/transition joint plans against the requested main segment geometry before any model write.
Use branches[*].branchSegmentSizes with one size per branch segment; networkPlan.branches[*].jointPlan reports transition expectations before apply.

Apply creates the main, branches, and accessories inside one TransactionGroup. Any branch, accessory, or semantic-verification failure rolls back the complete network; success reports atomicCommitSucceeded=true.

Accessory graph nodes are accepted in the request and surfaced in networkPlan. Apply supports duct/pipe accessory insertion hosted on a created main or branch segment with a compatible resolved family symbol and chainageFt/point, optionally loading an explicit workspace-scoped familyPath first, plus explicit target-id duct/pipe accessory delete and type_change with a compatible loaded type.

Accessory delete/type_change must provide targetElementId or targetElementIds. Type changes also require typeId, targetTypeName, familySymbolId, or familyName/typeName. Inserted accessories must match the route kind category.

tools.title: Reroute MEP Route Segment
tools.description: Guarded edit workflow for one straight duct/pipe curve. Discover candidates with /revit/find-elements includeGeometry:true and screen routeCurveCandidates before trial calls. A size-transition host must be at least 1.0 ft long so the transition can remain 0.5 ft from both ends. Current endpoint preservation requires exactly two physical End connectors and no side/tap Curve connectors; skip tapped hosts instead of weakening connection checks. Set operation:"offset" or operation:"size_transition" explicitly whenever size metadata is also supplied; omitted/auto preserves legacy inference. Offset mode derives two split points from host curve chainage or normalized chainage, reports replacement segments, offset points, selected type/system/level/size, and expected elbow fittings; offsetMode:"dogleg45" uses diagonal setback legs instead of perpendicular legs. Size-transition mode derives one transition point, reports upstream/downstream segment points, explicit selected sizes, and expected transition fitting. Apply replaces the host only after required fittings/connectors succeed, reports created segment/fitting ids, connector/system audit, endpointReconnectionPlan when applicable, and optional trace-enabled focused capture. Connected host endpoints are blocked by default; set preserveConnectedEndpoints:true only after dry-run reports a resolvable start/end endpointReconnectionPlan to reconnect the replacement route to original external endpoint connectors. Mutation flags are canonical: preview requires apply:false,dryRun:true; write requires apply:true,dryRun:false; omitted or equal pairs are rejected. Body offset: {operation:offset,kind:duct|pipe,hostElementId,split1ChainageFt?|split1Normalized?,split2ChainageFt?|split2Normalized?,offsetVector:{x,y,z},offsetMode?:orthogonal|dogleg45,doglegAngleDegrees?,preserveConnectedEndpoints?,apply,dryRun,verify?,visualVerify?,visualViewId?,focusPaddingFt?}. Body size-transition: {operation:size_transition,kind:duct|pipe,hostElementId,transitionChainageFt?|transitionNormalized?,upstreamDuctSize?|downstreamDuctSize?|upstreamDiameter?|downstreamDiameter?|upstreamPipeSize?|downstreamPipeSize?,sizePolicy?,preserveConnectedEndpoints?,apply,dryRun,verify?,visualVerify?,visualViewId?,focusPaddingFt?}.
tools.example: dry-run a 45-degree dogleg offset for isolated duct id 123

tools.title: Trace Connected Network
tools.description: Trace connected MEP elements via connectors starting from an element id. Body: {startElementId, systemName?, inferSystemFromStart?, stopAtBranchFittings?, stopAtTransitions?, maxHops?, excludeElementIds?, stopAtElementIds?, stopAtCategories?, includeDucts?, includePipes?, includeFittings?, includeAccessories?, includeTerminals?, includeEquipment?, includeOtherCategories?, maxElements?, includeSystemAudit?, systemAuditMaxElements?}. Returns connected ids grouped by category and ordered by traversal; includeSystemAudit optionally reports disconnectedIds = systemElementIds - connectedIds for duct and pipe systems.
tools.example: trace the connected duct run from this element

tools.title: Get Connectors
tools.description: Get connector identities, origins, sizes, directions, and optional flex duct/pipe control points and tangents for MEP elements. connectorIdBasis is revit_native_connector_id when the active Revit API exposes a durable connector ID; the enumeration_index_with_origin_guard_required fallback must be paired with the returned origin in repair requests. connectedTo preserves all Revit Connector.AllRefs entries; physicalConnectedTo excludes MEPSystem membership objects so isPhysicallyConnected and physicalConnectionCount can be used for actual topology/open-connector checks. Set onlyOpenPhysicalConnectors=true for a compact exhaustive scan that returns summary counts plus only open physical connector rows. Set includeVerificationParameters=true to read System Classification, Reference Level, Width, Height and Diameter in the same native callback as the full connector graph. This mode requires 1-500 unique positive elementIds, includeAllRefs and includeCoordinateSystem, and forbids open-only filtering. It returns verificationParameters with schema revit-operator.duct-verification-parameters/v1; missing fields remain explicit. Body: {elementIds:[...], includeVerificationParameters?, includeAllRefs?, includeCoordinateSystem?, includeFlexGeometry?, onlyOpenPhysicalConnectors?, maxConnectorsPerElement?}.

tools.title: Duplicate Type + Swap Instance

tools.title: Get Parameters

Omit schedule selectors to search bounded schedules; omit rowField to use standard identifier fields such as Mark, Number, Name, Designation, or DESIG. Defaults to dry-run unless apply:true.

tools.title: Export Visible Elements
tools.description: Export a mapped view image plus visible-element inventory on the same raster-consistent coordinate basis. Returns element ids, category/type/source/host context, explicit hostingSurface + link-host metadata, orientation payloads (facing/hand/basis/rotation), bbox/location geometry, image-space coordinates, visibleText for TextNotes/tags, and taggedSpatial for room/space tags in supported 2D views. Linked annotation tags use their transformed tag-head positions for frame inclusion, mapping, and geometry when a model bounding box is unavailable. Optional modelBounds:[minX,minY,minZ,maxX,maxY,maxZ] restricts host and transformed linked elements to an intersecting host-model box before the safety limit is applied. limit is 1..2000; page, filter categories, or use modelBounds instead of requesting a larger inventory. common_errors: View type is unsupported; export-visible-elements requires a crop-box-backed 2D view.
Crop box activation failed; activate crop in the target view or use export-view-region.

Supported for crop-box-backed 2D views only; use sheet-aware tools for DrawingSheet workflows.
categories/excludeCategories accept BuiltInCategory tokens and exact category names when tokens are unavailable.
includeLinked=true keeps link-scoped ids and transformed source/host/hostingSurface payloads so linked rows can be consumed without re-deriving host coordinates.
Orientation payloads include facing/hand vectors plus plan-azimuth and basis vectors when available; linked rows are transformed into host coordinates.
Mapping corners are emitted from the saved raster frame; crop-box corners are included only as reference metadata when the raster aspect differs.

No focus is applied to an earlier view. For a focused image, use export-image with exportMode=visible_region afterward. Elements absent from the requested view are returned in notShownElementIds with warnings; the handler does not invoke Revit's interactive closed-view search. Body: {viewId?|targetViewId?|sheetId?|id?|viewName?|query?,exact?,viewType?,showElementIds?,bboxMinXyz?,bboxMaxXyz?,zoomToFit?}.

Rename supports {action:"rename_types",familyName,searchPattern,replaceWith?,regexIgnoreCase?,maxEdits?,category|categories?,dryRun?}. Purge supports {action:"purge_unused_in_family",familyName,maxDelete?,category|categories?,dryRun?}.

Created resources may declare resultRef; later id fields may use '$resultRef' or '$action:N'. View crop uses cropBox:{min:{x,y,z?},max:{x,y,z?}}. Body: {actions:[...]}.

tools.title: View Visibility
tools.description: Read/update view settings. Actions: get, set_template, hide_category, show_category, set_scale, set_detail_level, set_discipline, set_phase, set_phase_filter, set_section_box, clear_section_box, set_crop_box, clear_crop_box, set_view_range, set_underlay, clear_underlay, set_category_override, clear_category_override, apply_view_filter, create_view_filter, remove_view_filter, clear_filter_override, isolate_elements_temp, isolate_categories_temp, clear_temp_hide_isolate, reveal_hidden_on, reveal_hidden_off, hide_elements, unhide_elements. get reports exact Plan View Range planes for plan views. set_view_range changes only supplied plane level/offset fields and dryRun executes a rolled-back native preview. get with includeLinkedModels:true reports loaded Revit links, common linked categories, linked phases, and phase-map rows when available. Linked-model category override requests block with linked_model_category_override_not_supported rather than changing host categories. set_crop_box supports annotationCropActive and annotationCropMarginFeet for tight sheet viewport extents. Supports linePatternId|linePatternName in category/filter overrides, and create_view_filter rule fields {ruleParameterName,ruleOperator,ruleValue,ruleCaseSensitive}.
tools.example: create and apply a view filter for supply ducts
notes: Use get with includeLinkedModels:true before linked-model graphics or phase mapping work; it reports Revit link ids/names, loaded document titles, common linked categories, linked phases, and phase-map rows when available.

Do not treat linkedModelName/linkName with set_category_override as a proven linked category override; Revit 2024 lacks a per-linked-category lineweight API in this handler, so those requests block with linked_model_category_override_not_supported instead of changing host categories.
set_crop_box accepts annotationCropActive and annotationCropMarginFeet; use them for sheet views so the viewport box does not include distant stray annotations.

set_view_range changes only supplied top/cut/bottom/view-depth level or offset fields; dryRun:true executes the native setter inside a rolled-back transaction and returns current plus proposed plane readback.
create_view_filter supports one-rule parameter filters and immediately applies the filter to the target view.

Use get with includeCategoryState:true and categoryName before and after hide/show category work. categorySnapshot reads all document categories/subcategories (maximum4096), reports exact target hidden/graphic attributes, and hashes all other direct category flags/graphic overrides in stable identity order. Require complete:true, equal categoryIdsSha256/count and otherCategoriesSha256, then compare target attributes; unsupported/failed reads remain unverified. This proves direct category state only, not effective element visibility or view-filter results.

tools.title: Create or Repair Text Note

Body: {action?,textNoteId?,viewId?,x?,y?,widthFt?,text?,typeId?|typeName?,newTypeName?,baseTypeId?|baseTypeName?,fontName?,textSize?,bold?,italic?,allowExisting?,dryRun?}. widthFt is paper-space feet, not model-space feet; create uses Revit's native line-wrapping overload and readback includes viewScale/modelSpaceWidthFt/isTextWrappingActive.
tools.example: create a note with controlled wrapping or repair its position, paper-space width, text, and type

tools.title: Export Elements to Excel Workbook (.xlsx)
tools.description: Export selected elements to an Excel spreadsheet under Workspace without changing Revit. Native typed values, units, display and field status in Elements, Issues and Readme. Use observed elementIds and exact parameterNames (max 2000 elements, 100 fields); inspect a representative element first. Optional supplementalTables preserve supplied inputs, proposed device quantities and review results, visibly assistant-authored with native identity columns. Each table requires every selected elementId exactly once; missing, duplicate or foreign rows reject before writing. Up to 4 tables, 32 columns each, 64000 total cells; scalar JSON values only (null is missing, zero remains zero, strings are not formulas). Body: {elementIds:[...],parameterNames:[...],outputFolder?,fileName?,dryRun?,supplementalTables:[{name,contentKind:'user_input_transcription'|'assistant_proposal'|'review',columns:[...],rows:[{elementId,values:[...]}]}]}. Supply all requested spaces and deliverables; native selection coverage is not proof of complete task scope or engineering correctness. Existing files are never overwritten. Verify artifact_receipt with inspect-exported-files.
tools.example: export selected elements and proposed quantities to xlsx

outputFolder.description: Prefer omitting this field: the default is artifacts/xlsx inside the Operator workspace. A supplied folder must be under that workspace; a relative folder is recommended. Documents, Downloads and other external folders are rejected before writing.

fileName.description: Simple unique workbook name, without directories. Existing destinations are never overwritten.

supplementalTables.description: Every table, including review, must contain each selected elementId exactly once. Include a review row even for an element with no issues; put general notes into those rows instead of adding duplicate element rows. Each row has one scalar value per column. Preserve explicit zero versus unknown null. Values are assistant-authored, not native or verified engineering facts. Across all tables: at most 64000 cells and 1000000 text characters.

tools.title: Tag Elements
tools.description: Create tags for elements by explicit ids and/or category selectors in a target view, with duplicate avoidance, optional per-category tag-type mapping, and additive geometry-aware placement/readback. geometry_aware places tag heads outside target footprints, avoids annotation/target/tag collisions, prefers clear plan space over walls and modeled equipment, keeps leaders bounded, rejects leader crossings and protected-content routes, uses discipline profiles, and requires actual Revit tag and leader geometry before retaining created work. Existing tags can be read or repaired in place with repairExistingTagId plus exact tag-head/free-leader coordinates; dry runs execute the native tag repair, read it back, roll it back, and verify the original tag geometry. If no compatible tag is loaded, autoLoadTagFamily can import an exactly category-compatible tag from a workspace-scoped source project, optionally selecting an exact source family/type; dry-run reports bounded source candidates. generatedTagContentProfile=airflow_only produces a copied source family that retains bounded flow-unit labels and removes unrelated text/label content, with an explicit sanitization receipt. A dry-run may set inspectTagFamilyElements=true to return a bounded read-only inventory of the selected tag family's internal elements and parameters. Tags with no visible/measurable head geometry or no professionally clear tag/leader route are removed and reported as failures. Create body: {viewId?|viewName?,elementIds?|categoryNames?,categoryTagTypeMap?,tagTypeId?|tagTypeName?|tagFamilyName?,onlyUntagged?,addLeader?,orientation?:horizontal|vertical,offsetX?,offsetY?,placementMode?:offset|geometry_aware,placementProfile?:auto|mep|electrical|architectural,tagWidthPaperInches?,tagHeightPaperInches?,clearancePaperInches?,maxRepairAttempts?,autoLoadTagFamily?,tagFamilySourceProjectPath?,tagFamilySourceCategory?,tagFamilySourceFamilyName?,tagFamilySourceTypeName?,generatedTagFamilyName?,generatedTagContentProfile?:none|airflow_only,inspectTagFamilyElements?,max?,dryRun?}. Existing-tag body: {viewId?|viewName?,repairExistingTagId,tagHeadPositionXyz?,leaderEndXyz?,leaderElbowXyz?,hasLeader?,leaderEndCondition?:attached|free,dryRun?}.

tools.description: Filters use {field|fieldId,op,value?,valueType?}; valueType is string (default), element_id, integer, double (Revit internal units), or display (field/document units). Resolve element IDs from current document evidence. Filter replacement is atomic; ambiguous field names require fieldId. Apply advanced schedule configuration (isItemized=false groups matching instances into summary rows; sort/group by type and airflow to keep different flows separate): fields, calculated fields/formulas, filters, sort/group, conditional formatting, field styling, appearance, filter-by-sheet, column widths, and row heights. Body: {scheduleId?|query?,addFields?,calculatedFields?,filters?,sortGroup?,showGrandTotals?,isItemized?,columnWidths?,rowHeights?,fieldFormats?,conditionalFormats?,appearance?,filterBySheet?,replaceFilters?,replaceSortGroup?,dryRun?}.
tools.example: configure a door schedule

tools.title: Delete Elements
tools.description: Delete elements by id.
tools.example: delete the selected elements

tools.title: Set Parameter
tools.description: Set element parameter values with post-commit readback. Each change may include expectedOldValue for an atomic in-transaction precondition; formatted Revit values such as 10,000 CFM are supported. If any expected value changed, the entire request returns Precondition Failed without writes. Body: {changes:[{elementId,parameterName,value,expectedOldValue?,preserveTextCase?}],dryRun?,apply?,confirm?,preserveTextCase?}. Applied responses report verifiedCount, verificationFailedCount, and unresolvedElementIds; inspect those fields before claiming success.
tools.example: set Mark on selected doors and verify the committed values

tools.title: Create Duct
tools.description: Create one straight duct segment from XYZ points or frame-linked view pixels through the verified MEP route engine. Explicit size is required. Native profile compatibility is checked before any transaction; ambiguous types require a native ductTypeId. Returns observed commit/rollback and geometry/size readback. For authorized creation use dryRun:false; use true only for a requested preview. Body: {levelName?,levelId?,startX?,startY?,startZ?,endX?,endY?,endZ?,frameId?,startPoint?,endPoint?,systemType?,ductType?,ductTypeId?,ductShape?:round|rectangular|oval,ductSize?|width?|height?|diameter?,dryRun?}.
tools.example: dry-run create a 10x12 supply duct segment from the marked line

tools.title: Create Pipe
tools.description: Create one straight pipe segment from XYZ points or frame-linked view pixels. Use dryRun first for redline/model-coordinate tasks. Body: {levelName?,startX?,startY?,startZ?,endX?,endY?,endZ?,frameId?,startPoint?,endPoint?,systemType?,pipeType?,diameter?|pipeSize?,dryRun?}.
tools.example: dry-run create a 2 inch domestic cold water pipe segment from the marked line

tools.title: Create Family Instance
tools.description: Place one or more family instances. Supports symbolName or typeName alias, optional levelName, target view/sheet placement (viewId|sheetNumber), spacing arrays (count + spacingX/Y/Z), rotationDegrees, and dryRun.
tools.example: place a north-arrow symbol on sheet A1.00
notes: symbolName or typeName is required.
For model families, x/y/z are absolute model-space feet, not offsets above the selected level. Native placement corrects and reads back the actual insertion point inside the transaction.
Verify every created ID with get-element-summary. It reports actual family/type/level and location.rotationRadians; the create response is not an independent verification.
viewId or sheetNumber can target view-specific/sheet annotation placement.
count + spacingX/Y/Z enables repeated placement in one call.

tools.title: Place Families
tools.description: Batch place family instances from a spec. Resolve the type by stable familySymbolId or familyName/symbolName. ViewBased symbols require viewId and use Revit's view-owner overload; apply fails closed unless readback proves the exact owner view, target-view collector membership, and a view-specific bounding box. Results include type, owner-view, requested and actual location, collector, and bounding-box evidence. For unhosted non-view-based instances, coordinateMode:absolute_model corrects any family-origin/level offset after creation and fails closed unless LocationPoint readback matches the requested XYZ exactly within tolerance. Non-view-based placement supports default levelName, optional per-instance levelName override, parameters, exact user-workset assignment by worksetName or worksetId, and explicit allowUnhostedWorkPlanePlacement for provisional work-plane families: without hostElementId this creates and retains a horizontal native reference plane at absolute requested XYZ, reports its supportPlaneElementId and verified effective level, and rolls both instance and plane back on failure/preview. This path defaults omitted coordinateMode to absolute_model and rejects legacy_level_offset or invalid modes. Ordinary omitted coordinateMode keeps legacy level-offset behavior. All coordinates use feet. Support is limited to 200 instances per request and is not an architectural ceiling. Orientation is returned from native rotation readback. For a linked ceiling, wall or floor, provide hostElementId for its RevitLinkInstance and linkedHostElementId for the exact linked element; linked-face placement checks both native host identities and the projected model-space point after regeneration. Unhosted work-plane placement is not a substitute for a requested ceiling host. Body: {familySymbolId?|familyName?,symbolName?,viewId?,levelName?,worksetId?,worksetName?,allowUnhostedWorkPlanePlacement?,dryRun?,bestEffort?,instances:[{x,y,z,coordinateMode?:absolute_model,levelName?,rotationDegrees?,hostElementId?,linkedHostElementId?,parameters?}]}.
tools.example: dry-run one view-based annotation symbol in the active detail view

allowUnhostedWorkPlanePlacement.description: Explicitly allows provisional WorkPlaneBased placement on a generated horizontal reference plane at the requested absolute XYZ. Retains and reports one support plane per created instance (maximum 200); this is not an architectural ceiling host. Preview and failed placement roll both back.

z.description: Feet; absolute model elevation in absolute_model mode, native level offset in ordinary legacy mode.

coordinateMode.description: Feet. absolute_model uses world XYZ. Omitted mode preserves legacy_level_offset for ordinary families; provisional unhosted WorkPlaneBased placement defaults to absolute_model and rejects legacy mode.

tools.title: Create Similar From Instance
tools.description: Create one or more hosted copies from an exemplar instance, preserving hosting behavior, orientation, and the exemplar workset with native verification while supporting exact host slots via wall-chainage or explicit point placements plus preview. Optionally match the source exemplar's electrical circuit. Before apply, inspect the source exemplar and include any instance parameters that drive visible tags or schedules in parameterNamesToCopy; geometry, host, and circuit agreement alone do not prove annotation fidelity. Body: {exemplarElementId,hostElementId?,roomId?|roomNumber?,roomSide?,referenceElementId?,alongHostOffsetsFt?|placements?,matchOrientationFromSource?,orientationSourceElementId?,copyRotation?,copyFacingHandState?,matchElectricalCircuitFromSource?,requireElectricalCircuitMatch?,parameterNamesToCopy?,parameterOverrides?,dryRun?,includePreviewImage?,previewViewId?,previewImageSize?,focusPaddingFt?}.
tools.example: dry-run create two similar receptacles from this exemplar on the same wall and keep them on the same circuit

tools.title: Move Elements
tools.description: Translate element(s) by vector or from/to points (supports dry-run). Set moveTogether:true with allOrNothing to translate a connected set in one native group call. Body: {ids:[...],mode:"vector",vectorX,vectorY,vectorZ,dryRun?,behavior:"allOrNothing"|"bestEffort",moveTogether?,options?}.
tools.example: dry-run move wall id 111 by -3ft in view-right
notes: Set moveTogether=true with behavior=allOrNothing to translate a connected set in one ElementTransformUtils.MoveElements call. moveTogether is incompatible with bestEffort.

tools.title: Rotate Elements
tools.description: Rotate element(s) around a vertical or arbitrary 3D axis (supports dry-run). Body: {ids:[...],angleDegrees,axis:{mode:"zThroughPoint"|"throughPoints",pointX,pointY,pointZ,endPointX?,endPointY?,endPointZ?},dryRun?,behavior:"allOrNothing"|"bestEffort",options?}.
tools.example: dry-run rotate an MEP fitting 90deg about its main-pipe axis
notes: axis.mode=zThroughPoint creates a vertical axis through (pointX,pointY,pointZ); throughPoints creates an arbitrary 3D axis from that point to (endPointX,endPointY,endPointZ).
